messages.subject: LPA results identical? Mplus vs MplusAutomation
messages.subject_clean: LPA results identical? Mplus vs MplusAutomation
messages.body_plain:
Hello everybody,

I have a probably ridiculous question, but I have to certainly rule this possibility out:
My task is to replicate the results of an alumni, who gave me his code and all the results. He used R with MplusAutomation. I use R and Mplus separately (admin issues, external server, 1 license, can't install anything etc...), but used his exact code.

Now, everything went well until a latent profile analysis with 13 variables and 46 observations (3-12 classes) does not converge at all (won't even after 10 h).
Is there any chance, that this happens, because I use Mplus separately instead of the package? Can MplusAutomation enforce any solutions?

I cannot imagine that this would make a difference and it seems ridiculous to me, but I would be grateful for an answer.

Thank you very much!
best regards,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] LPA results identical? Mplus vs MplusAutomation
messages.subject_clean: [MplusAutomation] LPA results identical? Mplus vs MplusAutomation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

MplusAutomation just creates data and runs the script through Mplus, so there should not  be any difference.  One thing I have had happen is data issues (either via MplusAutomation or Mplus directly) so that apparently identical scripts have different results.  (e.g., perhaps your colleague made the data and read it into R setting 9s to missing values from Rs end, so the data was just missing, but in the version of data you have they are actually 9s or some such).

Good luck finding a solution!

Cheers,

Josh

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] LPA results identical? Mplus vs MplusAutomation
messages.subject_clean: [MplusAutomation] LPA results identical? Mplus vs MplusAutomation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

I think Josh’s intuition about data issues (e.g., missing values) is a good one. Another possibility is that the model was previously run with a different version of Mplus and that something has changed under the hood in terms of estimation. I think that’s a long shot, but I have had rare experiences where model estimates or convergence changed across versions.

Also, the model you described (LPA with 13 variables, 46 observations, and 3-12 classes) sounds very underdetermined… you’ll end up with more parameters than cases very quickly, so that may have something to do with the nonconvergence.

Hope this helps,
Michael
